finding: The database connection has no read/write time limit. If the cloud database stalls on one request (connected but not answering), the app waits for ever. The 30-minute exit pass saves the book while it holds the mode lock, so one stuck save would freeze that pass; the next exit passes give up after 60 s thinking a rotation is running, and the next rotation waits for the lock with no limit. Stops and targets would then not be checked until the app restarts. The Den's database guard cannot help either: it measures a call only after the call returns. UNPROVEN that it has happened live; proven that nothing bounds it.
impact: EXIT - a single stalled database request can leave every open position without stop and target checks until a restart.
review_note: Confirmed against pymongo 4.17.0: the client computes socket_timeout None and CSOT None, so nothing bounded a read or a write; the five existing maxTimeMS guards are server-side aborts whose error still travels back over the same dead socket. WORSE than the row says: engine._open/_exit_half/_close are all @_book_lock, so the owner's own SELL button, the sector square-off and the Buy Desk freeze too - they cannot sell by hand to get out. Reproduced with no network (fake collection blocking on an Event, 56-position book, real save wrapper and real mode lock): the next exit pass stands down after 1 s, the rotation waits for ever, the book lock cannot be acquired, only a restart clears it. The silence was the log line asserting "rotation running - its own exit pass covers this slot", false on both halves; it now checks the holder and warns that stops and targets were NOT checked. 20 s is wide on purpose: the slowest single live call is ~half a second, and the 13.04 s statistics figure is ~25-30 round trips in a pass that is deliberately left unbounded. A NetworkTimeout IS a ConnectionFailure, so a breach lands in note_link_failure and the OPS-09 recovery already handles it.
proposed_fix: Give the client a socket and operation time limit (e.g. socketTimeoutMS 20000 and timeoutMS 30000) so a stalled request fails and the existing error paths take over.

finding: The danger leash floor silently narrows once a position's stop has risen above its entry price. engine._danger_pass computes the floor as the wider of 2.5%, the position's category stop and its ENTRY-STOP WIDTH, but it derives that width from the CURRENT stop_price under the guard `0 < stop < entry`. After one tighten on a winner the stop sits above entry, the guard fails, the width reads 0 and the floor falls to the category stop. Traced: a momentum position with a 12% ATR stop gets a 12% leash on the first danger day and a 5% leash on every one after.
impact: EXIT: a winning position is put on a leash less than half the width the owner accepted at entry, so an ordinary pullback stops it out of a winner. It cannot lose money below entry (the stop is above it), so this gives up upside rather than creating a loss.
